security_audit.summary: All static findings are false positives caused by Markdown documentation syntax and graphing terminology. The backtick matches are inline code or fenced examples, and the reconnaissance matches are ordinary terms like grid and solid. No prompt injection, network behavior, filesystem access, or external command execution was found in the reviewed files.

content.value_statement: Obsidian Desmos graphs can fail when parser syntax differs between settings, equations, and restrictions. This skill gives clear graph blocks, examples, and fixes.
actual_capabilities: Guides creation of desmos-graph code blocks for Obsidian notes.
Explains viewport, size, grid, axis labels, log scales, and default colors.
Shows functions, points, parametric curves, polar curves, and piecewise functions.
Documents colors, line styles, point styles, labels, restrictions, and special tags.
Troubleshoots parser errors for pi, square roots, pipes, colors, and polar equations.
Provides complete examples for trigonometry, curves, easing functions, and labeled points.
limitations: Does not install, configure, or modify the Obsidian plugin.
Depends on the obsidian-desmos plugin and its supported syntax.
Cannot confirm visual rendering without running Obsidian and the plugin.
Covers documented syntax from this source, not every Desmos feature.

use_cases.title: Prepare Math Lesson Notes
use_cases.description: Create graph blocks for functions, points, and transformations inside classroom Obsidian notes.

use_cases.title: Build Study Visuals
use_cases.description: Turn equations into styled Desmos graphs while avoiding common parser mistakes.

use_cases.title: Document Technical Models
use_cases.description: Add reusable graph examples for curves, restrictions, labels, and parameterized expressions.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Graph
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an Obsidian desmos-graph block for y=x squared and y=sin(x). Use different colors and simple viewport settings.

prompt_templates.title: Add Points and Labels
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a desmos-graph block with a cosine curve and labeled key points. Use correct LaTeX syntax for pi in point coordinates.

prompt_templates.title: Fix a Broken Graph
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my desmos-graph block for syntax problems. Check settings, equations, restrictions, colors, labels, and parser differences.

prompt_templates.title: Convert Advanced Curves
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a desmos-graph example for a polar curve that must be converted to parametric form. Include styling and safe restrictions.

output_examples.input: A user asks for sine and cosine graphs with a clear viewport.
output_examples.output: The skill returns a ready Obsidian graph block with two styled trig curves and matching bounds.

output_examples.input: A user asks why a point using pi does not render correctly.
output_examples.output: The skill explains that points require LaTeX pi syntax and rewrites the coordinate guidance.

output_examples.input: A user asks for a gray dashed helper line.
output_examples.output: The skill uses a supported hex color and applies the dashed style in the correct segment order.

best_practices: Use mathjs syntax in settings and LaTeX syntax in equations and points.
Use numeric values in restrictions when pi or square roots are involved.
Use supported color names or hex codes for every styled equation.
anti_patterns: Do not use LaTeX pi inside viewport settings.
Do not place pipe characters inside equation labels.
Do not use unsupported color names as style segments.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It helps create desmos-graph code blocks for interactive Desmos graphs inside Obsidian notes.

faq.question: Does it require the Obsidian Desmos plugin?
faq.answer: Yes. The generated syntax is intended for the obsidian-desmos plugin.

faq.question: Can it fix parser errors?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains common errors involving pi, square roots, restrictions, pipes, colors, and polar equations.

faq.question: Can it create labeled points?
faq.answer: Yes. It can show point syntax, labels, colors, and point styles.

faq.question: Does it run Desmos or Obsidian?
faq.answer: No. It provides syntax guidance and examples, but it does not render or execute the graph.

faq.question: Can it help with advanced curves?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for parametric curves, polar limits, piecewise functions, and restrictions.
